clue.text: Station worker? He's caught in odd pose

definitions.note: the question mark flags station in its Australian sense of a sheep farm

indicators.note: the pronoun is held inside the reworked letters, as a prisoner is caught
an odd arrangement of the word pose is a rearranged one

parts.note: the word as printed supplies the letters
the pronoun he, with 's (is) joining it to caught

explanation.surface: Someone poses strangely and a male figure gets trapped inside the awkward stance.
explanation.walkthrough: In Australia a station is a large sheep or cattle farm, which is why 'Station' points away from railways.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for a hand employed on a sheep station, a rural farm property.

clue.text: Special vessel with polish in to prepare for the theatre? (7, two words)

definitions.text: prepare for the theatre? (7, two words)

indicators.note: the polishing word sits inside the special vessel

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: A unique pot with polish inside, readied for the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' means the operating theatre, not the stage: surgeons wash thoroughly first.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wash hands and arms thoroughly before an operation, readying for surgery.

clue.text: Route march? Car met one, knackered (3 miles, they reckoned)

indicators.note: one stands for the answer itself: car met plus this one word together make the letters of route march
knackered means broken and worn out, so the letters of route march are rearranged once the named letters come out

explanation.surface: On a route march a car meets a worn-out walker who reckons on three miles.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUTE MARCH is an anagram of CAR MET plus the answer ('one'), so take CAR MET out and rearrange the rest. In older usage an hour was a distance, about three miles of walking.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour once served as a measure of distance, the ground covered on foot in that time, reckoned at about three miles.

clue.text: Fervent aunt, excited and filled with love for foundling (12, two words)

indicators.note: the excited letters have the zero placed inside them
excited letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: the two words as printed supply the letters
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A passionate aunt, all worked up and full of affection for a found baby.
explanation.definitionFit: French for a found child, an abandoned infant discovered and taken in by strangers.

clue.text: Oriental verse produced by e.g. Cinderella? I don't know what to say!

parts.note: Cinderella is a favourite Christmas pantomime

parts.words: I don't know what to say!
parts.note: um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A Christmas show produces Eastern poetry, leaving the spectator lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is the British Christmas family stage show, of which Cinderella is a classic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay verse form with interlinked repeating lines, adopted by French and English poets.

clue.text: Our deb, having come out, become hard, on the shelf?

definitions.note: on the shelf marks the verb as obsolete, put away

indicators.note: the debutante's coming out is read as the letters being let out and rearranged

parts.note: the two words as printed supply the letters

explanation.surface: Our debutante, after her society launch, grows hard-faced and ends up a spinster.
explanation.walkthrough: A deb comes out in society; 'on the shelf' means the word is obsolete, not unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete verb meaning to harden or make obstinate, related to obdurate.

clue.text: Docile dependent, one paid to appear in record

indicators.note: the payee is made to show up within the record, so those letters go inside

parts.note: a log is a written record, as of a voyage
the indefinite article a stands for one
pd is the bookkeeping abbreviation for paid

explanation.surface: A meek hanger-on turns up in the books as someone on the payroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a servile follower who meekly does another's bidding, like a pampered pet.

clue.text: Tropical fruit forming a ring in several pies

indicators.note: the ring sits inside the coin

parts.note: an anna was worth twelve pies, old Indian coins
the letter O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: An exotic fruit set in a ring of pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pies' are not pastries but small old Indian coins; twelve made an anna.
explanation.definitionFit: The custard apple or related fruit of the genus Annona, grown in hot climates.

clue.text: Stone that's green or black, set in crown, inverted

indicators.note: in a down clue, the whole is turned upside down
the gloomy word is mounted inside the crown, like a jewel

parts.note: the top of the head
black as in grim or dire

explanation.surface: A green or black gem mounted upside down in a royal crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black' sounds like a second colour for the stone, but it means dire, grim.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem variety of olivine, prized for its olive-green colour.

clue.text: Nervously evaded admitting one surrealist 'dull'?

indicators.note: the reworked letters let in the painter and his article
done nervously, the letters jitter into a new order

parts.note: the word as printed supplies the letters
an is a form of one
Salvador Dalí, the surrealist painter

explanation.surface: Someone dodged anxiously, letting in a surrealist who was boring.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something lifeless and monotonous, with no spark of activity.

clue.text: Torn in a way about title as mark of honour

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the title
in a way means in some form, loosely, so the letters of torn are rearranged

parts.note: a name can be a title, what something is called

explanation.surface: Someone is torn about accepting a title as an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: ORNT, an anagram of 'Torn' ('in a way'), goes round NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers allows ornament for an honour or decoration that adds distinction, like a medal.

clue.text: Good and indeed entertaining time for bairns

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold, so the time letter goes inside

parts.note: yes as an emphatic agreement

explanation.surface: A good, fun time for Scottish children.
explanation.walkthrough: Bairn is the Scots word for a child, which signals a Scots answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots plural for children, especially brats, matching the Scots word bairns.

clue.text: F. Bacon dispensed talk informally

indicators.note: dispensed as in dealt out freely, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the initial as printed
the surname as printed supplies the letters

explanation.surface: The philosopher Francis Bacon handed out casual chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'F. Bacon' reads as the Elizabethan writer's name, but the initial and surname are simply the letters to rework.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for having a chat, a shortening of confabulate.

clue.text: Cut discontinued lines, withering?

indicators.note: the Scots verb is stopped short, losing its final letter

parts.note: sneed, a variant of the Scots sned, means to lop or prune
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: Pruning back abandoned lines of plants, which are withering away.
explanation.walkthrough: Sned (also sneed) is a Scots and northern word for lopping branches.
explanation.definitionFit: Withering in the sense of scornful: given to curling the lip in contempt.

clue.text: Excitement as of old in Edinburgh to applaud the pope

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an obsolete word for an excited or exalted state
second meaning: Scots, to applaud by stamping the feet
third meaning: the ruffe, a small freshwater perch also called the pope

explanation.surface: An archaic thrill as Scots clap for a visiting pontiff.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: 'the pope' is not the pontiff but a fish, the ruffe, whose spelling here drops the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: One short word covers an old sense of passion, a Scots verb for stamping approval, and a perch-like fish.

clue.text: Opposed to worshipper eating

definitions.note: a heraldic adjective, so it matches the participle used adjectivally

parts.note: v. stands for versus, against
an orant is a praying figure in early Christian art

explanation.surface: Someone is against a churchgoer who is having a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: An orant is a figure shown with arms raised in prayer; the answer is a heraldic term.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, describing a beast shown devouring or swallowing something whole.

clue.text: Eccentric ideas about performing act creating stares

definitions.note: a noun phrase for the family that breeds stares, matching the plural Latin family name

indicators.note: the reworked letters go round the stage act
eccentric ideas are odd ones, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: the word as printed supplies the letters
a turn is a performer's act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: Weird notions about a stage routine that leave the audience gawping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stares' are not gazes but starlings: stare is an old word for the starling.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin family name for starlings and mynas, the birds a stare belongs to.

clue.text: Stringed instrument suggesting one of the winds?

definitions.meaning: a straight reading: an old bass instrument of the lute and cittern family
the cryptic reading: split as B, and, then three more letters, B joined to those letters spells the cold Adriatic wind

explanation.walkthrough: BANDORA reads as 'B and ORA', and B with ORA makes BORA, the bitter north-east wind of the Adriatic; 'the winds' sounds like an orchestra section.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixteenth-century plucked bass instrument of the cittern family, also spelt bandore.

clue.text: Soundboard made from a box I positioned with a television in

indicators.note: in means A and TV go inside the other letters
positioned means arranged, so the letters of box and I are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a soundboard from a box, with a television set inside.
explanation.walkthrough: BOXI rearranged ('positioned') gives BOIX; A + BOIX takes in A + TV after the B. An abat-voix is a sounding board above a pulpit.
explanation.definitionFit: An abat-voix is a canopy or sounding board above a pulpit that reflects the preacher's voice towards the congregation.

clue.text: A sitter in drag, as a taster?

indicators.note: the sitting member goes inside the sledge

parts.note: a sled is dragged along
the article taken as written
an MP sits in Parliament

explanation.surface: A portrait model in women's clothing, sampling the role.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sitter' sounds like an artist's model but is an MP, who sits in the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A past participle: tried out a small portion, offered as a trial.

clue.text: Unit put in reverse of trusty databank linking facility

indicators.note: the number is placed inside the reversed word
the word for trusty is taken backwards

parts.note: true means loyal and reliable
one is the unit number

explanation.surface: A component installed backwards in a reliable data network link.
explanation.definitionFit: A European online information network linking computer databases, as listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Latinate version of Aristophanes hit followed idea in translation?

parts.note: ran as a path ran along, followed, the river

indicators.note: the word is turned into another form, rearranging its letters

parts.note: the word as printed supplies the letters

explanation.surface: The Latin rendering of a Greek comedy hit came after a translated idea.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristophanes' hit 'The Frogs' gets a Latinate equivalent in the zoological family name.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoological family of true frogs, a Latin form recalling Aristophanes' comedy The Frogs.

clue.text: Stall? Six secured by long lock

indicators.note: the number is held inside the hair

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Delay tactics, as six are fastened by a long bolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' is the noun, a partition between horses, not the verb meaning delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A partition between stalls in a stable, or the stall itself, as Chambers lists.

clue.text: Indian vessel dad brought to English river

indicators.note: the father is placed up against the river, joining it at the front

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
the Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall

explanation.surface: Father carried a boat from India to a river in England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river forming most of the Devon–Cornwall border in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A lateen-rigged coasting boat used off the western coast of India.

clue.text: Wandering spectre, headless, image repetitively developed

indicators.note: letters that wander are moved out of order
the ghost loses its first letter

parts.note: the ghost's name as printed supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A roaming ghost without its head, its picture printed over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychological term for a mental image formed by repeated perception of similar objects.

clue.text: More than half of date palm chopped for timber

indicators.note: chopped up letters are cut into a new arrangement
five of the eight letters of the tree's name are kept

parts.note: the tree's name as printed supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Most of a date palm is chopped down for wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the last five of the eight letters in 'date palm', then rework them.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard pale wood of a familiar deciduous tree, used for furniture and flooring.

clue.text: Malarial fever's hard, but not on odd-toed mammal

parts.note: tap is an Indian word for malarial fever, with 's joining it

indicators.note: the word for hard drops the two letters spelling on

parts.note: iron, as in hard as iron

explanation.surface: A tough bout of malaria, but not one that affects an odd-toed beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofed animal of the order of perissodactyls, which have an odd number of toes.

clue.text: Feeling a bit of a yen and stuff

parts.note: a sen is a hundredth of a yen
to sate is to fill full

explanation.surface: A craving, a small longing, and a lot of things alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like a longing but is the Japanese currency, of which the sen is a small fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for perceiving through the senses, so endowed with sensation.

clue.text: Extract of copra taken in a wine — banned antibiotic

parts.note: the article taken as written

indicators.note: the reworked letters are absorbed inside the French word for wine

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: what is extracted is drawn out and remade, so the word copra is rearranged

parts.note: copra, dried coconut kernel, supplies the letters as printed

explanation.surface: Coconut oil drawn off and mixed into wine as an outlawed drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Copra is dried coconut kernel; 'Extract' sounds like the oil but signals the letters being remade.
explanation.definitionFit: A glycopeptide growth promoter for livestock, prohibited in the EU over fears about resistant bacteria.

clue.text: Angle on growing plant showing sickliness with times taken inside?

indicators.note: the multiplication sign is taken into the word

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell
x is the multiplication sign

explanation.surface: A poorly plant looks sickly, having had frequent indoor spells.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical term for the angle between a leaf and the stem it grows from.

clue.text: Boiler stuffed with soft octopus

indicators.note: the hen has the letter for soft put inside it, as stuffing

parts.note: a boiler is a hen for boiling, French poule
p for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A cooking pot filled with tender octopus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boiler' looks like a pot but is a boiling fowl, a hen, French poule.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-derived name for the eight-armed cephalopod, also spelt poulp.

clue.text: Statement by previous speaker from southern states (short of English)

indicators.note: the southern name lacks the letter for English

parts.note: Dixie is a nickname for the US South

explanation.surface: Remarks from the last talker, from the American South, without an English accent.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is Latin for 'I have spoken', used to close a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin formula meaning I have said it, closing a speech already given.

clue.text: Fifty-one'll require humour sharing the same pad

parts.note: LI is fifty-one in Roman numerals, with 'll (will) joining it to require
a vein is a mood or humour, as in a jocular vein

explanation.surface: A fifty-one-year-old will need some jokes to share a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pad' is slang for a flat or home.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for a partner or employee who resides in the same home.

clue.text: Short verse inscribed in capital portico?

indicators.note: the verse is written inside the capital's name, as on a monument

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France
v is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A brief poem carved into the porch of a building in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is fair because the word means an enclosed space before a church, sometimes a portico.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed court or colonnaded porch in front of a church or cathedral entrance.

clue.text: Room with seats in annexe (draughty)

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters across these two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of annexe and the start of draughty

explanation.surface: A sitting room in a chilly annexe.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical recess or room with seating, used for conversation, as in Greek houses.

clue.text: Nasty weather returning about start of winter — chimneys not in use?

indicators.note: the whole is read the other way, going back
the icy weather goes round the initial

parts.note: sleet is unpleasant wet snow

indicators.note: the first letter of winter

parts.note: the season's first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Bad weather comes back as winter begins, while the hearths sit cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in use' marks an obsolete word: a tewel was a flue or chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic plural noun for flues or smoke vents, so obsolete chimneys.
